interactionPlan.concept: A multilayer perceptron (MLP) transforms input data through alternating operations of linear mixing and element-wise non-linear activations.
learningObjectives: After engaging with this figure, the student will understand how network diagrams map to mathematical equations for neural networks.
The student will be able to explain the visual distinction between fully-connected linear layers (crossed arrows) and element-wise activations (straight arrows).
interactionPlan.keyInsight: In a network diagram, crossing arrows show where features are mixed together via weights (matrix multiplication), while parallel straight arrows show operations applied independently to each feature (like ReLU).

interactions.label: Trace Forward Pass
interactions.effect: Highlights the nodes and edges corresponding to the specific stage of computation, fading the rest of the network.
interactions.teaches: The sequential, layer-by-layer nature of feedforward neural network computation.

demo_steps.title: The Input Data
demo_steps.narration: Notice the white nodes on the far left. These represent the raw input features (x1, x2) of a single datapoint entering the network.
demo_steps.focus: The leftmost column of white nodes labeled x1, x2.

demo_steps.title: Mixing Features (Linear Layer)
demo_steps.narration: Follow the crossed arrows from the inputs to the first hidden nodes (z11, z12). The criss-crossing indicates that every input feature is multiplied by a weight (W1) and added together, mixing the data to form new pre-activations.
demo_steps.focus: The crossed arrows labeled W1 and the gray nodes z11, z12.

demo_steps.title: Independent Activations
demo_steps.narration: Now look at the straight horizontal arrows moving from z to h. These represent an element-wise activation function, like ReLU. Notice they don't cross—the function is applied to each node independently to introduce non-linearity.
demo_steps.focus: The straight parallel arrows between the z1 and h1 columns of gray nodes.

demo_steps.title: Deep Transformations
demo_steps.narration: This alternating pattern repeats! The network applies another linear transformation (W2) followed by another activation to create deeper, more abstract representations (h2) of the original data.
demo_steps.focus: The sequence from h1 through W2 to the second set of z and h nodes.

demo_steps.title: Generating Predictions
demo_steps.narration: Finally, the last set of crossed arrows (W3) maps the deep features to the output layer (y1, y2). These white nodes typically represent the final predictions, like class probabilities in a softmax regression.
demo_steps.focus: The final crossed arrows labeled W3 and the rightmost white nodes y1, y2.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Layout 6 columns of circular nodes horizontally. Column 1: two white nodes (x1, x2). Col 2: two gray nodes (z12, z11). Col 3: two gray nodes (h12, h11). Col 4: two gray nodes (z22, z21). Col 5: two gray nodes (h22, h21 - correct the typo from the original image which repeated h1). Col 6: two white nodes (y2, y1). Draw fully-connected crossed arrows between Col 1->2, Col 3->4, and Col 5->6. Draw straight horizontal parallel arrows between Col 2->3 and Col 4->5. Add bold labels W1, W2, W3 below the crossed arrow sections with vertical ellipses above the W to indicate connection bundles.
